title: Merge many CSV files into one

explanation.text: A common job: you get one CSV file for each month (`2026-01.csv`, `2026-02.csv`, and so on) and you want **one table** with everything, so you can add things up. Python can do this in a few lines.
**Step 1: find the files.** `Path(".").glob("*.csv")` gives every CSV file in the folder. Use `sorted(...)` so the order is always the same.
Name your files **year-month**, like `2026-01.csv`. Then sorting the names also sorts the months in time order. With names like `jan.csv` and `feb.csv`, February would come before January.
**Step 2: read each file and add a column.** After you merge, you can no longer see which file a row came from. So add a `month` column from the file name.
**Step 3: use the merged table.** Now it is a normal list of dictionaries. Add up amounts per month, per product, or per customer.

items: A file has the columns in a different order. `DictReader` does not mind: it uses the column names.
A file is missing a column. Use `row.get("amount", "0")` so one bad file does not stop everything.
Every file has its own header line. With `DictReader` you read each file separately, so headers are not copied by mistake.
Amounts are text. Turn them into numbers with `float(...)` before you add them.

explanation.title: merge all monthly files
explanation.text: Put your monthly files in a folder named monthly. Run this next to it. It writes a new file all_months.csv and never changes the originals. Use copies of your files the first time.
explanation.code:
import csv
from pathlib import Path

rows = []
for path in sorted(Path("monthly").glob("*.csv")):
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            row["month"] = path.stem
            rows.append(row)

if not rows:
    raise SystemExit("No CSV files found in the monthly folder.")

# Collect every column name that appears in any file, keeping the first-seen order.
columns = []
for row in rows:
    for name in row:
        if name not in columns:
            columns.append(name)

with open("all_months.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=columns, restval="")
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(rows)

print("Merged", len(rows), "rows into all_months.csv")

quiz.question: Why name monthly files like `2026-01.csv`?
options: Sorting the names also sorts the months in time order
quiz.explanation: With year first, alphabetical order is also time order. `feb.csv` would come before `jan.csv`.

quiz.question: Why add a `month` column when you merge?
options: To remember which file each row came from
quiz.explanation: After merging, the file name is gone. A `month` column keeps that information.

quiz.question: A file has no `amount` column. What keeps the script from crashing?
quiz.explanation: `.get` gives a default value when the key is missing, so one odd file does not stop the job.
